en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Eleventh Chapter
The Discourse on the Stability of the Dhamma:
Is the stability of the Dhamma (dhammaṭṭhitatā) fully accomplished (parinipphanna)?
Yes, it is.
Is that state of stability fully accomplished?
One should not say so … [as before] … Is that state of stability fully accomplished?
“Yes,” you say.
“But by that very [practice], there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, and no final Nibbāna without clinging—is that so?
You must not speak thus… [and so on].
Is the stability of form fully accomplished?
Yes. Is that stability itself fully accomplished? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is that state of being established (ṭhitatā) fully accomplished (parinipphanna)? Yes.
By that very [state], is there no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round, and no final Nibbāna through non-clinging?
One should certainly not say so …pe… [the same applies to] the stability of feeling …pe…
Is the stability of perception …pe… the stability of volitional formations …pe… the stability of consciousness an ultimate reality?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is that which exists by way of such existence (ṭhitatā) fully established (parinipphanna)?
You should not say so … [and so on] …
Is that state of being established something fully accomplished? Yes.
If so, by that very state there is no making an end of suffering, no cutting off of the round of existence, and no final Nibbāna through non-clinging?
It should not be stated thus... [etc.
...The Discussion on the Stability of Dhamma is finished.
